claim: The cortical network model comprises 211,712 neurons in 2.4 mm³ of tissue.
source: For this study, we used a seven column subvolume comprising 211,712 neurons in 2.4 mm3 of tissue (Figure 1A).
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript describing the model specifications.

claim: Excitatory cells are modeled as a diverse set of morphologies with conductances distributed across all electrical compartments.
source: In line with the biological variability, excitatory cells are modeled as a diverse set of morphologies (Reimann et al., 2024a; Kanari et al., 2019; Figure 1B) equipped with conductances distributed across all electrical compartments (Reva et al., 2023; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Direct statement supported by citations and reference to figures showing morphological diversity and conductance distributions.

claim: Plasticity acted sparsely and specifically during simulated evoked activity.
source: During simulated evoked activity, plasticity acted sparsely and specifically, although it was still able to reorganize the network's dynamics, manifesting in more pattern-specificity after plasticity.
evidence: Direct statement summarizing simulation results.

claim: Potentiation dominated in amplitude and depression counteracted it in frequency, leading to stable firing rates without homeostatic terms.
source: Potentiation dominated in amplitude and depression counteracted it in frequency, which led to stable firing rates without explicitly introducing any homeostatic terms (Zenke et al., 2017a; Turrigiano and Nelson, 2004).
evidence: Direct statement with citations to relevant literature on homeostatic plasticity.

claim: Plasticity was driven by co-firing cell assemblies, spatial clustering of synapses on dendrites, and the centrality of a connection in the network.
source: We found plasticity was driven by the network topology beyond pairwise connectivity. Specifically, by co-firing cell assemblies, spatial clustering of synapses on dendrites, and the centrality of a connection in the network.
evidence: Direct statement summarizing key findings about drivers of plasticity.

claim: The predictions were confirmed in the MICrONS dataset, an openly available electron microscopic reconstruction.
source: Furthermore, we confirmed our testable predictions in the (MICrONS, 2021) dataset, an openly available electron microscopic reconstruction.
evidence: Direct statement about validation in external dataset.

claim: The calcium-control hypothesis postulates that prolonged, moderate amounts of Ca2+ lead to depression while large transients lead to potentiation.
source: The calcium-control hypothesis, put forward by Lisman, 1989 postulates that prolonged, moderate amounts of Ca2+ lead to depression (a decrease in efficacy) while large transients of Ca2+ lead to potentiation.
evidence: Direct statement with citation to the original hypothesis.

claim: The NMDA receptor is the molecular substrate of Hebbian coincidence detection.
source: The molecular substrate of Hebbian coincidence detection is the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor, which upon removal of the Mg2+ block by depolarization, conducts Ca2+(Mayer et al., 1984).
evidence: Direct statement with citation to experimental evidence.

claim: Depolarization-induced entrance of calcium into the postsynaptic dendrite is important to evoke changes in synaptic efficacy.
source: By putting these together, it became evident that it is not necessarily the timing of the postsynaptic spike, but rather the depolarization induced-entrance of calcium into the postsynaptic dendrite that is important to evoke changes in synaptic efficacy (Goldberg et al., 2002; Lisman and Spruston, 2005).
evidence: Direct statement with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Excitatory firing rates remained stable throughout the entire 10-minute simulation.
source: To assess the stability of our network while undergoing plasticity with our specific choice of calcium-based rule, we simulated 10 min of biological time of in vivo-like, stimulus-evoked network activity and verified that excitatory firing rates remained stable throughout the entire length of the simulation (Figure 2C).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing firing rate stability.

claim: The STDP rule kept inducing the same magnitude of changes throughout all 10 minutes of the simulation instead of stabilizing after a transient phase.
source: We observed that the STDP rule kept inducing the same magnitude of changes throughout all 10 min of the simulation instead of stabilizing after a transient phase (Figure 2E, pink line).
evidence: Direct statement comparing STDP to calcium-based rule with reference to figure.

claim: The calcium-based plasticity rule promotes stability in the network.
source: In summary, the calcium-based plasticity rule promotes stability in our network.
evidence: Direct summary statement of findings.

claim: The number of connections changing was below 18% across the whole network.
source: Indeed, we found that the number of connections changing was below 18% across the whole network and remained low when restricted to individual layers (Figure 3A1).
evidence: Direct statement with specific percentage and reference to figure.

claim: The propensity of changes increased as the pairwise firing rates increased.
source: Moreover, the propensity of changes increased as the pairwise firing rates increased (Figure 3A2), in line with previous modeling insights (Litwin-Kumar and Doiron, 2014; Graupner et al., 2016).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure and citations to supporting literature.

claim: Depression was more common than potentiation at both the connection and synapse levels.
source: On the level of individual synapses changes were even sparser (Figure 3B1), and in both cases, depression was more common than potentiation.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure.

claim: Layer 5 pyramidal cells contributed mostly to changes on the basal dendrites, while apical changes happened mostly on Layer 6 pyramidal cells.
source: Layer 5 (L5) PCs contributed mostly to changes on the basal dendrites, while apical changes happened mostly on L6 PCs (Figure 3B2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing layer-specific changes.

claim: The mean value of peak AMPA conductance decreased minimally (-2 pS) due to plasticity.
source: We found a minimal decrease (–2 pS, Figure 3C1) in its mean value due to plasticity, which was explained by frequent depression and a heavy tail of potentiation amplitudes (Figure 3C2).
evidence: Direct statement with specific value and reference to figures.

claim: 60% of potentiation and 40% of depression crossing the unstable fixed-point occurred within the first minute.
source: Furthermore, the vast majority of these crossings occurred early, with 60% of potentiation and 40% of depression happening within the first minute (Figure 3D2).
evidence: Direct statement with specific percentages and reference to figure.

claim: Random Poisson spikes without spatio-temporal structure reduced the number of connections undergoing plasticity by 25%.
source: We ran control simulations where we delivered random Poisson spikes on the same VPM fibers with the same mean rate, but without the spatio-temporal structure of the stimuli. We found that this reduced the number of connections undergoing plasticity by 25%, demonstrating the importance of stimulus structure over simple firing of pre- and postsynaptic neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct statement with specific percentage from control simulation.

claim: The plasticity model is not strictly Hebbian, since postsynaptic firing alone could change synaptic efficacy, although presynaptic release was required for most changes.
source: Thus, our plasticity model is not strictly Hebbian, since the effect of postsynaptic firing alone could change synaptic efficacy, although presynaptic release was required for most of the observed changes (Graupner and Brunel, 2012; Graupner et al., 2016).
evidence: Direct statement with citations to supporting literature.

claim: The amount of plastic changes between layers differed from those expected in a random control with the same pre- and postsynaptic populations.
source: In particular, we found layer-to-layer pathway specificity in the amount of plastic changes observed. That is, the amount of changes between layers differed from those expected in a random control with the same pre- and postsynaptic populations (Figure 4A2 vs. Figure 4A3).
evidence: Direct statement comparing to random control with reference to figures.

claim: There was strong overexpression of simplices in the subgraph of changing connections compared to the control.
source: We found strong overexpression of simplices in the subgraph of changing connections compared to the control (Figure 4B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing simplex counts.

claim: The maximal simplex dimension found in the subgraph exceeded the value expected by chance by two.
source: Furthermore, the maximal simplex dimension found in the subgraph exceeded the value expected by chance by two.
evidence: Direct statement about simplex dimension analysis.

claim: Approximately 7% of synapses undergo long-term plasticity under realistic in vivo-like conditions in 10 minutes of biological time.
source: In summary, we observed that ∼7% of synapses undergo long-term plasticity under realistic in vivo-like conditions in 10 min of biological time, and most of these synapses are on L5 PC's basal dendrites.
evidence: Direct summary statement with specific percentage.

claim: Functional assemblies were activated in all stimulus repetitions and a series of three to four assemblies remained active for 190 ± 30 ms.
source: Functional assemblies were activated in all stimulus repetitions and a series of three to four assemblies remained active for 190 ± 30 ms (Figure 5B).
evidence: Direct statement with specific timing and reference to figure.

claim: Up to 13.8% of synapses depressed when restricting analysis to assemblies, compared to 5% in the whole dataset.
source: While only 5% of synapses depressed in the whole dataset, we found up to 13.8% when restricting the analysis to assemblies.
evidence: Direct statement with specific percentages comparing assembly vs. whole dataset.

claim: Up to 5.2% of synapses potentiated when restricting analysis to assemblies, compared to 2% in the whole dataset.
source: Similarly, compared to 2% of all synapses potentiating, we observed up to 5.2% when restricting to functional assemblies.
evidence: Direct statement with specific percentages comparing assembly vs. whole dataset.

claim: Synapses across assemblies underwent more plastic changes than synapses within assemblies.
source: Interestingly, large values were found in the off-diagonal entries (Figure 5F), i.e., synapses across assemblies underwent more plastic changes than the synapses within these assemblies.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing within vs. across assembly changes.

claim: Co-firing in a Hebbian cell assembly is a better predictor of plastic changes than just firing at a high rate.
source: In conclusion, co-firing in a Hebbian cell assembly is a better predictor of plastic changes than just firing at a high rate.
evidence: Direct conclusion statement based on comparison with rate-based controls.

claim: Cells that fire together more than expected have three times higher chances of changing the efficacy of their synapses under in vivo-like conditions.
source: Our contribution lies in making the qualitative statement above into a quantitative one: Under in vivo-like conditions, cells that fire together more than expected have three times higher chances of changing the efficacy of their synapses.
evidence: Direct quantitative statement summarizing findings.

claim: Clustered synapses within early and middle assemblies were unlikely to undergo plastic changes.
source: Surprisingly, clustered synapses within an assembly were only likely to undergo plastic changes in the larger, but less general late assembly, A11, but not in early and middle assemblies (Figure 6C black arrows top).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing likelihood analysis.

claim: Non-clustered within-assembly synapses were the most likely to change across all assemblies.
source: In fact, the only category that was likely to change across all assemblies is that of non-clustered within-assembly synapses.
evidence: Direct statement about likelihood of changes across categories.

claim: Clustered, within-assembly synapses depress to a significantly smaller degree than all other categories.
source: However, when comparing not the likelihood, but the amplitude of changes across categories with a two-way ANOVA, we found that clustered, within-assembly synapses depress to a significantly smaller degree than all other categories (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Direct statement with statistical test and reference to figure.

claim: Cross-assembly synapses that were part of a spatial cluster were likely to be initiated as fully depressed and had a high chance of undergoing potentiation.
source: Here, the picture was reversed: cross-assembly synapses that were part of a spatial cluster were likely to be initiated as fully depressed and then had a high chance of undergoing potentiation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C black arrow).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing cross-assembly analysis.

claim: The indegree of the pre- and postsynaptic neurons of a connection are predictive of plastic changes.
source: Furthermore, the indegree of the pre- and more strongly of the postsynaptic neurons of a connection are predictive of plastic changes (Figure 7B1).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing indegree analysis.

claim: As k-edge indegree increased, the probability of undergoing plastic change increased across dimensions.
source: Across dimensions, as k-edge indegree increased so did the probability of undergoing plastic change (Figure 7C2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing k-edge indegree analysis.

claim: Among connections that change, those with the highest k-edge indegree tend to get potentiated while those with the lowest favor depression.
source: Furthermore, among the connections that change, the ones with the highest k-edge indegree tend to get potentiated while those with the lowest favor depression (Figure 7C3).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing conditional probabilities.

claim: High k-edge indegree led to higher connection strength in the MICrONS dataset, as predicted by the modeling insights.
source: Indeed, high k-edge indegree led to higher connection strength in MICrONS, 2021 as predicted by our modeling insights; moreover, the curves across dimensions are qualitatively the same for both datasets (Figure 7D).
evidence: Direct statement comparing model predictions with MICrONS data with reference to figure.

claim: The probability of changes only increased with k-edge indegree in the assembly sub-graph associated with the presented pattern or to a late assembly.
source: More precisely, the probability of changes only increased with k-edge indegree in the assembly sub-graph associated with the presented pattern or to a late assembly and that it was the strongest for the former (see Figure 7E2 left for pattern A for an example, right for a summary of the maxima attained for all patterns, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B for consistency across repetitions of the same simulation).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figures showing pattern-specific analysis.

claim: Firing rates decreased slightly as a result of plasticity.
source: Firing rates decreased slightly as a result of plasticity (Figure 8A left), while spike correlations remained stable, in line with recent findings (Oby et al., 2019; Feulner et al., 2022, Figure 8A right).
evidence: Direct statement with citations and reference to figure.

claim: The highest correlations both before and after plasticity were found in the most central edges in the network.
source: However, the highest correlations both before and after plasticity were found in the most central edges in the network i.e, those with highest edge participation in high-dimensional simplices (Figure 8B1).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing correlation analysis.

claim: This prediction about central edges having highest correlations was verified in the MICrONS dataset.
source: We further verified this prediction in the MICrONS dataset (Figure 8B2, see Methods).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing MICrONS validation.

claim: An early assembly responding to patterns B and E before plasticity split into two stimulus-specific assemblies after plasticity.
source: While we found considerable overlap between assemblies detected before and after plasticity, an early assembly responding to patterns B and E before plasticity, split into two stimulus-specific assemblies (Figure 8C).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing assembly splitting.

claim: Assembly sequences responding to repetitions of a given pattern generally became more reliable after plasticity.
source: Moreover, the assembly sequences responding to repetitions of a given pattern generally became more reliable after plasticity (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing reliability analysis.

claim: Hamming similarity of assembly sequences between repetitions showed significant increases for most patterns after plasticity.
source: To quantify this, we measured the Hamming similarity of assembly sequences between repetitions and found significant increases for most patterns (see Methods, Figure 8D).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to methods and figure showing statistical analysis.

claim: The increase in assembly-level reliability contrasted with a slight decrease in the reliability of neuronal activity on the single cell level.
source: Interestingly, this increase on the assembly level lied in contrast with a slight decrease in the reliability of the neuronal activity on the single cell level (Figure 8E).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure showing single-cell reliability.

claim: The plasticity mechanism can contribute to the emergence of a robust population code with unreliable neurons.
source: This shows that the plasticity mechanism can contribute to the emergence of a robust population code with unreliable neurons.
evidence: Direct interpretive statement based on findings.

claim: Plasticity can make circuit responses more distinct between stimuli by increasing specificity but also less distinct for a given stimulus by increasing reliability.
source: Crucially, this means that plasticity can make circuit responses more distinct (between stimuli by increasing specificity) but also less distinct (for a given stimulus by increasing reliability).
evidence: Direct interpretive statement based on findings.

claim: The calcium-based rule evolves an over-excitable network towards lower excitability.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that the calcium-based rule evolves an over-excitable network towards lower excitability, which in this case is a role that a homeostatic rule would play (Turrigiano and Nelson, 2004; Zenke et al., 2017a).
evidence: Direct summary statement with citations to homeostatic plasticity literature.

claim: The model used a seven column subvolume of rat non-barrel somatosensory cortex (nbS1).
source: To study how plasticity and various network level features interact to explain structure-function relationships, we used a bio-realistic, large-scale cortical model of the rat non-barrel somatosensory cortex (nbS1).
evidence: Direct statement describing the model system.

claim: The current model improves on Markram et al., 2015 in terms of both anatomical and physiological properties.
source: The current model improves on Markram et al., 2015 in terms of both anatomical, e.g., atlas-based cell composition and placement (described in Reimann et al., 2024a), and physiological properties, e.g., improved single-cell models, multi-vesicular synaptic release, and layer-wise compensation for missing synapses (described in Isbister et al., 2023).
evidence: Direct statement with citations describing model improvements.

claim: Thalamic input was delivered via fibers from the ventral posteriomedial nucleus (VPM) and the posteriomedial nucleus (POm).
source: To deliver input with spatio-temporal precision to the circuit, we used thalamic fibers from the ventral posteriomedial nucleus of the thalamus (VPM) and the high-order posteriomedial nucleus of the thalamus (POm; Figure 1D; Meyer et al., 2010).
evidence: Direct statement with citation and reference to figure.

claim: Ten VPM input patterns were repeatedly presented in random order with a 500 ms inter-stimulus interval, together with non-specific POm input.
source: In short, 10 VPM input patterns were repeatedly presented in random order with a 500 ms inter-stimulus interval, together with a non-specific POm input.
evidence: Direct statement describing stimulus protocol.

claim: VPM patterns were defined with varying degrees of overlap in the sets of activated fibers.
source: These VPM patterns were defined with varying degrees of overlap in the sets of activated fibers (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 4; see Methods).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figures.

claim: Spontaneous activity was driven by somatic injection of a layer- and cell-type-specific noisy conductance signal.
source: Spontaneous activity was driven by somatic injection of a layer- and cell-type-specific noisy conductance signal (Isbister et al., 2023, see Methods).
evidence: Direct statement with citation.

claim: An estimated 12 million core hours were required to run all simulations presented in the manuscript.
source: Although deep profiling of all campaigns was not done, an estimated 12 M core hours were required to run all simulations presented in the manuscript.
evidence: Direct statement about total computational cost.

claim: Simulations were always repeated at least three times to assess the qualitative consistency of the results.
source: Simulations were always repeated at least three times to assess the qualitative consistency of the results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct statement about simulation replication with reference to figure.

claim: 8% of Layer 6 pyramidal cells could not be made to fire a single action potential (only bursts), so synapses on those cells were assumed to be non-plastic.
source: Since 8% of L6 PCs could not be made to fire a single action potential (only bursts), synapses on those cells (10,995,513 in total) were assumed to be non-plastic, i.e., their thresholds were set to a negative value that could not be crossed.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section.

claim: Connections between Layer 4 spiny stellate cells were made non-plastic because their plasticity was shown to be non-NMDA dependent.
source: Similarly, as the plasticity of connections between L4 spiny stellate cells was shown to be non-NMDA dependent (Chindemi et al., 2022; Egger et al., 1999) those connections were made non-plastic.
evidence: Direct statement with citations in Methods section.

claim: Spikes were binned using 20 ms time bins for assembly detection.
source: First, spikes of excitatory cells were binned using 20 ms time bins (Harris et al., 2003).
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section with citation.

claim: Time bins with significantly high firing rates were determined as crossing a threshold defined as the mean activity level plus the 95th percentile of the standard deviation of 100 shuffled controls.
source: Second, time bins with significantly high firing rates were determined as crossing a threshold defined as the mean activity level plus the 95th percentile of the standard deviation of 100 shuffled controls.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section.

claim: The MICrONS dataset is an electron microscopic reconstruction of a large volume of cortical tissue.
source: We confirmed our testable predictions in the MICrONS datasets, an openly available electron microscopic reconstruction of a large volume of cortical tissue.
evidence: Direct statement in Abstract.

claim: The minnie65_public release of the MICrONS dataset contains 60,048 classified neurons.
source: For the comparison of two of our findings with a rodent electron microscopy dataset with co-registered calcium-imaging traces, the minnie65_public release of the (MICrONS, 2021) dataset was used. Synapses from sources other than one of the 60,048 classified neurons inside the bigger (minnie65) volume were discarded.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section.

claim: Eight calcium-imaging sessions from the MICrONS dataset were used, with at least 1000 neurons scanned in each session and at least 85% co-registered in the structural data.
source: For the functional dataset, eight calcium-imaging sessions from the 661 version were used. These sessions were selected by the same criteria as in Reimann et al., 2024b; Santander et al., 2024, namely at least 1000 neurons were scanned in each session and at least 85% of them were co-registered in the structural data.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section with citations.

claim: The MICrONS functional dataset included 243 neurons per session on average, totaling 1817 unique neurons.
source: Deconvolved spike trains of neurons (243 neurons/session on average, 1817 unique neurons in total, 2% and 15% of all cells, respectively) were used to calculate Pearson correlations.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section.

claim: Spike time reliability was defined as the mean of the cosine similarities of a neuron's mean-centered, smoothed spike times across all pairs of repetitions of a single pattern.
source: Spike time reliability was defined as the mean of the cosine similarities of a given neuron's mean-centered, smoothed spike times across all pairs of repetitions of a single pattern (Schreiber et al., 2003; Cutts and Eglen, 2014).
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section with citations.

claim: Spike times were binned to 1ms time bins and convolved with a Gaussian kernel with a standard deviation of 10ms for reliability analysis.
source: To smooth the spike times, they were first binned to 1ms time bins, and then convolved with a Gaussian kernel with a standard deviation of 10ms as in Ecker et al., 2024; Santander et al., 2024.
evidence: Direct statement in Methods section with citations.

claim: The model is based on an early developmental stage (P14-16: juvenile rats).
source: However, L5 TTPC bursts were rare in our simulations, as the model is based on an early developmental stage (P14-16: juvenile rats) and firing bursts only becomes prominent as the animals mature (Zhu, 2000).
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion with citation.

claim: The extracellular magnesium concentration of 1 mM used in in vitro preparations was assumed to be representative of the in vivo level.
source: Third, the extracellular magnesium concentration of 1 mM used in in vitro preparations was assumed to be representative of the in vivo level.
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion listing model assumptions.

claim: The model uses data from juvenile rat non-barrel somatosensory cortex, sometimes supplemented with data from barrel cortex, adult animals, and mouse due to lack of high-quality source data.
source: A common limitation of data-driven modeling is the lack of high-quality source data, thus while we refer to our model as juvenile rat non-barrel somatosensory cortex, sometimes we used data from the barrel cortex, from adult animals and from mouse.
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion acknowledging data limitations.

claim: The model does not include inhibitory plasticity, metabotropic glutamate receptors, neuromodulation, slow homeostatic plasticity, structural plasticity, or calcium-induced calcium release.
source: Finally, learning in the brain is orchestrated by several mechanisms in unison and some of these are beyond the scope of this paper, e.g., inhibitory plasticity, metabotropic glutamate receptors, neuromodulation, slow homeostatic plasticity, structural plasticity, and calcium-induced calcium release (Magee and Grienberger, 2020).
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion listing mechanisms not included with citation.

claim: Adding biological complexity allowed reduction in the number of mechanisms explicitly modeled.
source: Thus, we showed that adding biological complexity allowed us to reduce the number of mechanisms explicitly modeled.
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion about modeling philosophy.

claim: The model and detailed instructions to launch simulations and analyze results are open-sourced.
source: To facilitate further research, we are open-sourcing our model alongside detailed instructions to launch simulations and analyze the results (see Data and code availability).
evidence: Direct statement in Discussion about data availability.

claim: Previous theoretical work showed that embedding simple STDP rules in spiking networks without fast homeostatic plasticity leads to exploding firing rates.
source: Previous theoretical work has shown that while embedding simple STDP rules in spiking networks without fast homeostatic plasticity leads to exploding firing rates (Morrison et al., 2007; Zenke et al., 2017a), this is not necessarily the case for calcium-based rules (Higgins et al., 2014; Graupner et al., 2016; Chindemi, 2018; Wang and Aljadeff, 2022).
evidence: Direct statement with citations to theoretical literature.

claim: Calcium-based rules do not necessarily lead to exploding firing rates unlike simple STDP rules.
source: Previous theoretical work has shown that while embedding simple STDP rules in spiking networks without fast homeostatic plasticity leads to exploding firing rates (Morrison et al., 2007; Zenke et al., 2017a), this is not necessarily the case for calcium-based rules (Higgins et al., 2014; Graupner et al., 2016; Chindemi, 2018; Wang and Aljadeff, 2022).
evidence: Direct statement with citations to theoretical literature.

claim: The model demonstrates that not only the scale of the network and biorealistic connection probabilities contribute to stability, but also the use of a calcium-based plasticity model.
source: This demonstrates that not only the scale of the simulated network, its biorealistic connection probabilities and the low, in vivo-like rates contribute to the stability of changes observed in our simulation, but also the use of a calcium-based plasticity model (Chindemi et al., 2022) in line with previous modeling insights (Higgins et al., 2014).
evidence: Direct interpretive statement with citations.

claim: The firing rate flipped from synchronous to asynchronous within a minute of biological time.
source: Surprisingly, the firing rate flipped from synchronous to asynchronous (Figure 2F, right) and it did so within a minute of biological time (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figures.

claim: Pattern C elicited the strongest response while pattern H elicited the weakest.
source: Pattern C elicited the strongest response, while pattern H the weakest, and the responses of patterns H and I were the most similar to each other, as expected, since they share 66% of the VPM fibers (Figure 2A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure.

claim: Patterns H and I had the most similar responses because they share 66% of the VPM fibers.
source: Pattern C elicited the strongest response, while pattern H the weakest, and the responses of patterns H and I were the most similar to each other, as expected, since they share 66% of the VPM fibers (Figure 2A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure explaining similarity.

claim: Early assemblies are stimulus-specific and not part of the same assembly sequences.
source: As early assemblies are stimulus-specific, and thus not part of the same assembly sequences, synaptic depression between these cells can be seen as some kind of stimulus separation.
evidence: Direct interpretive statement based on data.

claim: Late assemblies are mostly non-specific and participate in all assembly sequences.
source: These functional assemblies are mostly non-specific and participate in all assembly sequences, thus the potentiation of their efferents means a general strengthening of the stimulus response as a whole.
evidence: Direct interpretive statement based on data.

claim: Stable early assemblies can function as a stable backbone amid ongoing synaptic plasticity.
source: These stable early assemblies can therefore function as a stable backbone amid ongoing synaptic plasticity.
evidence: Direct interpretive statement based on findings.

claim: Synapses between assemblies are more likely to change, especially if they form a cluster on the postsynaptic dendrite.
source: Together with the previous results, this suggests that synapses between assemblies are more likely to change, which is even more pronounced if these synapses form a cluster on the postsynaptic dendrite.
evidence: Direct summary statement based on cross-assembly analysis.

claim: Simplex motifs innervating a cell have been shown to be a good predictor of assembly membership.
source: Second, simplex motifs innervating a cell have been shown to be a good predictor of assembly membership (Ecker et al., 2024), which in turn have an effect on plasticity as demonstrated above.
evidence: Direct statement with citation.

claim: Both the nbS1 model and MICrONS dataset had similar maximal dimensions of simplices and ranges of k-edge indegree values.
source: Both networks had similar maximal ddimensionsof simplices as well as ranges of k-edge indegree values (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), making the results of this analysis comparable.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure comparing datasets.

claim: Total synapse volume was used as a measure of connection strength in the MICrONS dataset.
source: For MICrONS, we used total synapse volume of a connection (see Methods), as a measure of connection strength (Harris and Stevens, 1989).
evidence: Direct statement with citation.

claim: Pattern-indegree is the number of VPM fibers belonging to a pattern that innervate a neuron.
source: Finally, pattern-indegree, i.e., the number of VPM fibers belonging to a pattern that innervate a neuron, is also a good predictor of the probability of a connection to change i.e., an increase of either the pre- or postsynaptic pattern-indegree of a connection leads to more frequent plastic changes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C11).
evidence: Direct definition with reference to figure.

claim: Correlations of connected pairs of neurons decreased slightly after plasticity following the decrease in firing rate.
source: Correlations of connected pairs of neurons decreased slightly after plasticity following the decrease in firing rate (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure.

claim: Both firing rate effects and correlation effects were more pronounced in the deeper layers.
source: Both of these effects were more pronounced in the deeper layers (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figure.

claim: While Markram and Tsodyks, 1996 showed redistribution of synaptic efficacy at the single connection level in vitro, this study found redistribution at the network level under in vivo-like conditions.
source: Thus, while Markram and Tsodyks, 1996 showed a redistribution of synaptic efficacy after plasticity at the single connection level in vitro (Figure 8F), we found a redistribution at the network level under in vivo-like conditions (Figure 8A-D, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Direct comparative statement with citation and references to figures.

claim: The model observed a network-level redistribution of synaptic efficacy that maintained spike correlations globally while enhancing stimulus-specificity and reliability of subpopulations.
source: In summary, we observed a network-level redistribution of synaptic efficacy that maintained spike correlations globally, while enhancing stimulus-specificity and the reliability of the subplopulations in terms of assembly activation.
evidence: Direct summary statement of findings.

claim: The most central connections of the network drive the correlated activity, a prediction confirmed in the MICrONS dataset.
source: Furthermore, we derived and confirmed in the (MICrONS, 2021) dataset a prediction stating that the most central connections of the network drive the correlated activity.
evidence: Direct statement about prediction and validation.

claim: The model's principal observations include that plastic changes were sparse (affecting only 7% of synapses), non-random, and stimulus-specific.
source: Our principal observations are as follows: (1) Plastic changes were sparse, affecting only 7% of the synapses. A balance between occasional, large-amplitude potentiation and more frequent depression stabilized the network without explicitly modeling homeostatic plasticity. Moreover, the changes were non-random and stimulus-specific.
evidence: Direct summary statement in Discussion.

claim: Plastic changes were largely determined by anatomical structure of synaptic connectivity and its relation to functional units.
source: (2) Plastic changes were largely determined by the anatomical structure of synaptic connectivity and its relation to functional units, i.e., changes were most likely between co-firing cell assemblies, at clustered synapses, between neurons highly innervated by the same input, and in central edges in the network.
evidence: Direct summary statement in Discussion.

claim: While assemblies remained fairly stable, they became more stimulus-specific and reliable.
source: (3) While assemblies remained fairly stable, they became more stimulus-specific and reliable which has important implications for coding and learning.
evidence: Direct summary statement in Discussion.

claim: The model is not designed to solve any specific task but is a model of sensory cortex that learns to represent stimulus features in an unsupervised manner.
source: Note, however, that despite the comparison to machine learning, our model is not designed to solve any specific task. Instead, it is a model of sensory cortex which only learns to represent stimulus features in an unsupervised manner.
evidence: Direct clarification statement in Discussion.

claim: Demonstrating stimulus-specificity of changes and increased reliability of assembly sequences was crucial validation that results have implications for learning.
source: Nonetheless, demonstrating the stimulus-specificity of changes as well as an increase in the reliability of assembly sequences, was a crucial validation that our results are not just a description of a biophysical process, i.e., plasticity, but have implications for learning in general.
evidence: Direct interpretive statement in Discussion.
